title: Resilience spectra: establish guardrails for idempotent contracts and hedged orchestration across SDKs/runtime
creator: Asha Patel
description: Problem: Services and client SDKs currently use inconsistent retry, timeout, and backoff behavior. This causes unpredictable tail latency, doubled work due to unsafe retries for non-idempotent operations, and hard-to-debug multi-region failovers. Goal: Define a compact, actionable resilience 'spectra' — a set of standard guardrails (timeouts, retry counts, backoff profiles, hedged request rules, idempotency contract, circuit-breaker defaults, and load-shedding signals) that can be implemented in both the runtime and official SDKs. The guardrails must: 1) respect per-route SLOs and latency budgets, 2) allow safe retries for idempotent operations, 3) support optional hedged requests when latency SLOs are at risk, 4) enable multi-region failover with controlled fanout, and 5) provide observability hooks and migration path from current behavior.
acceptance_criteria: A short spec published that maps SLO class -> timeout/retry/backoff/hedge/circuit-breaker defaults
SDKs (Node and Python) implement the baseline config with telemetry, feature-flagged for rollout
Runtime supports an override API: per-route resilience profile + canary rollout ability
Idempotency header contract documented and integrated into SDK request helpers
End-to-end test harness simulates region outage and verifies bounded request duplication and SLO preservation
Dashboards added: per-route retry rate, hedged-request rate, duplicate-response rate, and critical path latency percentiles
decisions: Use three SLO classes: latency-critical (P99 <= 150ms), standard (P99 <= 500ms), throughput-first (best-effort)
Default retry window is conservative: no retries for non-idempotent endpoints; single idempotent retry with exponential backoff for standard class
Hedged requests enabled only for latency-critical class and only in the runtime; SDK exposes opt-in helper for client-side hedging
Circuit breaker defaults: error threshold 5% over 1m for production; short open timeout (30s) with linear backoff on subsequent opens
Load-shedding signal is a boolean header + metrics emitted by runtime; SDKs will surface a 503 variant and recommend recommended fallback flows
Idempotency keys are first-class: SDK helper to generate v1 keys and runtime enforces dedup window by default (30s)
Backoff profiles: bounded exponential (base=200ms, cap=2s) for standard retries; tight profile for latency-critical (base=20ms, cap=200ms) when hedging disabled
plan: Draft spec and mapping table for SLO class -> resilience profile (this ticket)
Design runtime API (resilience_profile override) and storage for dedup entries (LRU with TTL)
Implement SDK helpers: idempotency key generator, safeRetry wrapper, optional client-side hedge API
Add telemetry hooks and trace spans for hedged calls, retry attempts, dedup matches, and circuit-breaker transitions
Create canary rollout: start with internal services in us-west2 auto-scaling pool; enable hedging only behind feature flag
Run chaos tests: simulated region latency spikes and partial network partitions
Iterate on thresholds based on measured duplication and cost impact; finalize defaults and document migration guidance
progress_updates: 2025-02-12: Kickoff meeting with SRE, runtime, and SDK leads. Agreed on three SLO classes and that idempotency is required for retries.
2025-02-20: Initial draft of mapping table reviewed by Maya Gupta (SRE) and Ethan Ross (runtime). Main comment: hedging cost needs budgeting per-customer tier.
2025-02-28: Prototype SDK safeRetry wrapper landed in feature branch (github.com/redwood/runtime-sdk/pull/314). Node + Python versions created.
2025-03-03: Runtime dedup cache prototype integrated into request pipeline; basic TTL-based dedup working for idempotency keys.
2025-03-05: Design review: agreed to add observability labels for customer-tier and route, and to surface hedging cost estimate in Console
migration_and_rollout: Phase 1 (internal canary): enable standard profiles for internal services only. Monitor duplication rate and cost delta for 2 weeks.
Phase 2 (partner rollouts): invite 3 high-traffic customers to opt into hedging for latency-critical routes behind feature flag.
Phase 3 (general availability): flip default conservative retries in SDKs; runtime default profiles enforced unless customer overrides.
Fallback: allow per-customer runtime opt-out and per-route feature flags during rollout
observability_and_metrics: New metrics: runtime.retry_attempts_total, runtime.hedged_requests_total, runtime.duplicate_responses_total, runtime.dedup_hit_ratio
Traces: ID-annotated spans for hedged siblings with hedged.parent and hedged.sibling attributes
Dashboards: per-route P50/P95/P99 latency before/after hedging, cost per million tokens for hedged operations, dedup ratio
Alerts: sudden increase in duplicate_responses_total OR sustained hedged_requests_total > 1% of total calls triggers P1 review
testing_and_validation: Unit tests for SDK safeRetry ensuring no retries on unsafe methods by default
Integration tests that replay idempotent requests and assert dedup behavior within TTL
Chaos test: inject 200-500ms tail latency in us-east-1 and measure hedged success rate and added GPU cost
Game-day: simulate full region outage and validate failover does not double-execute non-idempotent workflows
security_considerations: Idempotency keys are stored in dedup cache; keys must not leak PII. SDK helper warns about including user data in keys.
Dedup cache encryption at rest and access control enforced in private deployments
notes_and_tradeoffs: Tradeoff: aggressive hedging reduces tail latency but increases cost and potential duplicate side-effects; we limit hedging to latency-critical routes and opt-in.
Tradeoff: longer dedup windows reduce duplicate work but increase memory for dedup cache; default set to 30s with per-route override.
Compatibility: older SDKs without idempotency helpers will continue to function but will be subject to no-retry defaults for safety
